subject.affected_artifact: Candidate Implementation Plan v0.2; not approved

scope_inspected: §2 repository/architecture context and conflicting persistence statements
IP-01 and IP-02 task targets, prerequisites, and completion criteria
observations: §2 says the API owns validation, authentication/authorization, scope, orchestration, contracts, job submission, and persistence.
The same §2 says API/presentation must not own persistence, worker, Azure, provider, or secret-management concerns.

§6 lists a .NET Web API/application logical target separately from a domain/application and persistence boundary, without defining how those responsibilities relate or where storage-specific implementation is owned.

IP-01 establishes the API solution/quality baseline; IP-02 establishes .NET domain/application contracts, a persistence boundary, Azure SQL schema and migrations. Neither task resolves the conflicting wording.

§5 places IP-02 after IP-01 and identifies persistence contracts as cross-cutting prerequisites; §7 contemplates SQL repositories and persistence integration testing but does not resolve architecture ownership.
§1 states v0.2 is a Draft Candidate, not Human Plan Approved, and not authorized for implementation.
source_inspection.classification: Direct source inspection; not product execution.

scope_inspected: §9 API and Integration Requirements and final-contract language
observations: §7 assigns the .NET 8 Web API persistence responsibility and separately identifies Azure SQL as the relational data store.
§8 says entities are logical and not a finalized schema; indexes, foreign keys, retention and tenant-aware uniqueness are design-time implementation matters.
§9 says endpoint names are examples and final schemas, validation, status/error behavior, needed idempotency, and OpenAPI documentation are to be defined.
